title: May the Force be with You: A Tulpa Creation Guide (v2.8.1)
author: Methos (@GGMethos)
edition_cited: V2.8.1, PDF formatting by u/NeoMahler; OCR text from archive.org item 'tulpamancy'
locator_hints: closing lines of Part 6 on 'flash imposition' and 'blink imposition'
summary: Part 6 of this guide gives the author's own route to seeing an imagined companion in real space. He insists imposition comes last, after the figure speaks and acts unexpectedly, and says it 'occurs naturally' after long time spent. Method: picture the figure walking in front of you (not behind) through the day with a constant gait; then sit daily for a few hours with the figure in full view, examining it from different angles and distances in real space and having it move in patterns; work on peripheral vision. He names 'blink imposition' and 'flash imposition' (short bursts of concentrated visualization) as variants, stresses belief, and reports sound imposition took him two weeks while touch and sight took far longer, 'up to hundreds of hours'. Links two tulpa.info forum guides for visual and touch imposition.
why_relevant: First-person community instruction for open-eye imposition with stated durations and sequence; shows the 'it comes naturally with hours' view against the stepwise methods of other guides.

date_evidence.basis: title block of the document prints 'V2.8.1 / Last Edit: 28-Sep-2017'; independently, archive.org stamps the containing item 'tulpamancy' addeddate 2020-04-14

notes: Licensed CC BY 4.0 per its own licence page, so full text is saved; still treated as in copyright for quoting (paraphrase plus anchor). Whether the result is actually seen or 'pretended' is left loose in places: he writes 'pretend that your tulpa is walking beside you'; the reader should judge mode carefully.
